    🌊 Oceanism¶

    "On land we limp. Under water we are what the world intended."

    Oceanism is the faith of the Yaoma Tribe — the mermaid-like Yaoma who inhabit two islands south of Zakarutia and east of Xobkua's western sea. It teaches that ocean creatures are perfect — finished by the world as it was meant to be — while land creatures, including humanoids who breathe air, are drafts, sketches, early errors the world is still correcting. To be Yaoma is to live on the shoreline between perfection and its rough draft.

    Oceanism is not a sect of Kirivs-bin. The Yaoma honor Kirivis as a brave land-general, but their scripture is the tide.

    Origins¶

    Oceanism has no prophet and no founding date. Yaoma song-history encodes it as always-present: when the first Yaoma egg hatched in warm shallows, the hatchling already knew that water was home and air was exile.

    The faith's narrative form emerged as the Yaoma Tribe built its dual-island polity: one island for habitation (surface structures, beaches, egg-shallows) and one sacred atoll for governance, where only the Tide-Council (seven elders chosen by the phases of Maenar and Amelia) may tread. Around ~200 BGD, the council's song-keepers codified disparate tide-songs into the Perfect Ocean Cycle — the complete Oceanist canon: a sequence of melodies that, sung in order over a lunar cycle, tells the faith entire.

    The Yaoma are sometimes called "marmots" in Asatru traders' pidgin (a corruption of merfolk via marmot). Yaoma find this hilarious and occasionally adopt it ceremonially — "the marmots of the perfect ocean" — to puncture mainland solemnity.

    Beliefs¶

    • Ocean creatures are perfect — not metaphorically. A dolphin's hydrodynamics, a shark's electroreception, a coral's colonial architecture — these are finished forms. A Yaoma song-scroll catalogues hundreds of such perfections as verses of scripture. Perfection here means fitting — the creature fits its medium without remainder.
    • Land creatures are drafts — mammals in particular are compromises: they carry their ocean (blood, amniotic fluid) inside them because they left it incompletely. Demons, humans, orcs, giants — all walk on legs that the world has not yet solved. This is not contempt but melancholy: land-dwellers are "still worth singing to," Yaoma say.
    • The shoreline is purgatory — Yaoma themselves live in the border between perfect and draft. They water-breathe but build on beaches; they lay eggs in shallows but conduct diplomacy on atolls. Their islands are liturgical reminder that perfection is adjacent, visible a fin-kick away, but not theirs to inhabit full-time while politics requires legs.
    • Song is how perfection remembers itself — Yaoma songs travel miles underwater, serving simultaneously as communication, history-keeping, and art. An elder who can sing their lineage back a thousand years is Oceanism's closest analogue to a priest — not intercessor but living archive.
    • Pearls as prayer-knots — imperfect irritants transformed into perfections by patient nacre. Yaoma pearl-diving is thus both economy and liturgy; a flaw tolerated long enough becomes beauty.

    Practices¶

    • Tidal magic as devotion — Yaoma mages command currents, summon storms, and converse with sea creatures; their magic is strongest at high tide, weakest at low. To work tidal magic well is to demonstrate that you understand perfection's rhythm.
    • Egg-shallows guarding — eggs laid in warm shallows are guarded communally, with the tribe singing the Perfect Ocean Cycle over them for the full incubation. A clutch sung to completely is considered Oceanist-baptized.
    • Atoll silence — the governance atoll is Oceanism's most sacred space and its quietest. No song-scroll is performed there; only the natural lap of water on coral. To legislate in silence is to remember what perfection sounds like when no one is composing it.
    • Salvage as recovery — Yaoma divers recover artifacts from sunken vessels across the southern strait. Each recovered object is catalogued as "a draft returning to water" — not treasure but repentant matter.
    • Beaching vigil — a young Yaoma beaches themselves for up to two hours at sensory limit — gills drying, tail aching — to feel, somatically, why land is unfinished. Rescuers wait with wet kelp; the vigil ends with reimmersion and communal song.

    Relation to Kirivs-bin¶

    Not a sect. A parallel.

    • Oceanism does not venerate Kirivis as normative. Kirivis is honored as "the land-general who saw the conspiracy" — impressive for a draft, but not binding on a tide-faith.
    • Where Kirivs-bin says honor is earned, Oceanism says perfection is given (to ocean creatures) and practiced toward (by shore-dwellers). Different anthropology.
    • Where Kirivs-bin says action is prayer, Oceanism says song and tide-keeping are prayer — notably less individualist: no Yaoma sings alone; songs require water as medium and other Yaoma as chorus.
    • Asatru theologians classify Oceanism as a "marine folk faith" — Yaoma hear this as "draft-language for a perfection you haven't learned to breathe in." Relations are courteous but theologically incommensurable.

    Yaoma who live in mainland port enclaves (trading pearls, coral, and salvage) often observe both Oceanism and, socially, Kirivs-bin festivals without conflict — the sea does not mind what you do on shore, as long as you remember where the perfection is.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Yaoma Tribe — universal among Yaoma; Tide-Council is both government and synod
    • Islands: two islands + sacred atoll south of Zakarutia, east of Xobkua; seabed gardens and song-corridors between them are also considered Oceanist "territory" though no map marks them
    • Avoidance: the Glub Kingdom — intelligent slimes unsettle Yaoma; the idea of an amorphous land-jelly that can reshape at will is, in Oceanist terms, "a draft that refused to choose a perfection"
    • Trade presence: Yaoma pearl and salvage networks carry Oceanist song-fragments and pearl-knots throughout the Demon Continent south; mainland demons prize Yaoma-harvested pearls without understanding they are prayer-beads
